_meta.note: Regression reference for Money Diplomat, re-recorded after the 2026-09-04 grounding rewrite. The v1 golden was discarded: its expected output carried confidence percentages, resentment_risk, culture_clash_risk, the_real_issue, emotional_stakes, if_guilt_trip, what_splitting_signals, likely_outcome and likely_counteroffer — every one of which the new schemas removed. The money-profile and monthly-recap endpoints are gone entirely and their cases with them. Re-run with `npm run check:golden money-diplomat`. The north star, and what to read for by eye: the tool is strongest answering 'what is fair or prudent here, given what I actually know, and what can I say?' and weakest answering 'what is this person secretly thinking?', 'what will happen?', 'what does my culture require?' or 'what number is objectively correct?'. Reason about the money, help with the conversation, do not invent the people. Each case carries its own `guards` line. See audit/tool-notes/MONEYDIPLOMAT-NOTES.md.

cases.name: lend-overdue-first-loan
cases.guards: The case in the owner's PDF. The first loan is overdue and undiscussed; that is the strongest supplied fact and the whole answer should rest on it. NOTHING may predict repayment, forecast resentment, or say the friendship will suffer. The holiday booking may appear as a bare fact in what_is_known but must never be read as evidence about their finances — 'why the first loan has not been repaid' and 'what the holiday says about their finances' belong in what_is_not_known. recommendation is pinned to exact English because the frontend colours on it.

input.situation: A friend is asking to borrow $400. I lent them $600 about eight months ago which was supposed to be paid back within three months and never was. We have not talked about it since. They just posted about booking a holiday.
input.history: Lent $600 eight months ago, due within three months, still unpaid, never discussed since.

why: The existing $600 loan is five months overdue and has never been discussed, so the earlier debt remains unresolved.
Adding a new loan before addressing the first one means you would have $1,000 outstanding with no agreement in place on either amount.
There is no supplied information about why the first loan was not repaid or when it might be, which makes the terms of any new loan impossible to set clearly.
what_is_known: You lent your friend $600 approximately eight months ago.
Repayment was due within three months, meaning it is now roughly five months overdue.
The overdue loan has not been discussed since it was made.
Your friend is now asking to borrow an additional $400.
Your friend recently posted about booking a holiday.
what_is_not_known: Why the $600 has not been repaid.
Whether your friend is aware you consider it overdue.
Your friend's current financial situation or capacity to repay either amount.
Whether your friend intends to raise the earlier loan themselves.
before_you_decide: Do you want the $600 back, or have you quietly written it off?
Are you comfortable having $1,000 outstanding with this person if the new loan also goes unpaid?
Do you want to raise the earlier loan before responding to this request?

if_you_lend.amount_guidance: Given the unresolved $600, lending anything additional before that debt is acknowledged would mean accepting real uncertainty about both amounts. If you decide to lend after discussing the earlier loan, keep the new amount to whatever you could genuinely afford to lose.
terms_to_clarify: Acknowledge the existing $600 and agree on a repayment plan for it first.
Set a specific repayment date for the new amount in writing or by message.
Agree whether the two amounts will be repaid together or separately.
if_you_lend.script: Hey, before I respond to this I want to check in about the $600 from earlier in the year — it has been a while and we never really talked about it. Can we figure out a plan for that first? Once we sort that out I am happy to talk about what else I can help with.

if_you_do_not_lend.script: I am not in a position to lend right now, sorry. I also think we should find a moment to talk about the $600 from earlier — I do not want it to just sit there between us.
if_you_do_not_lend.if_they_push: I really cannot right now. I hope you can sort it out another way.

existing_debt.next_step: Raise the $600 directly before responding to the new request. You do not need to know why it was not repaid to ask about it — the fact that it is overdue is enough to bring it up.
existing_debt.script: Hey, I want to be straightforward with you — the $600 I lent you was meant to come back around five or six months ago and we have not talked about it. I would like to figure out where things stand before anything else.

cases.name: venmo-three-weeks
cases.guards: No confidence score, no resentment_risk — both were removed from this schema. The verdict is pinned English. Nothing may predict whether asking damages the relationship.

input.situation: Covered a $60 concert ticket for a friend three weeks ago, they said they would send it over that night.

why: There was a clear, same-night repayment agreement — this is not an ambiguous loan.
Three weeks have passed without the agreed payment, which is a reasonable threshold to follow up.
$60 is meaningful enough that letting it go without a word sets a precedent you may not want.
what_matters: The explicit promise to pay that night makes this a missed commitment, not a forgotten favor.
Whether your friend has reached out at all about the delay — you did not mention any follow-up from them.
Whether this is a pattern or a one-off lapse in this friendship.
unknowns: Whether your friend has a reason for the delay they have not communicated.
Whether there has been any contact between you since the concert that touched on this.
output.script: Hey, just a quick reminder — I covered your concert ticket a few weeks back and you mentioned sending the $60 that night. No big deal, just want to square it up. Venmo, cash, whatever works for you.
output.if_they_push_back: Totally understand if things are tight right now — just let me know when works and we can sort it out then. I just want to make sure it does not fall through the cracks.

cases.name: afford-sparse-numbers
cases.guards: Cost and income only. gut_check must NOT be 'Looks manageable' on this alone — what_is_missing should be substantial, because cost and income are insufficient for a real affordability answer. No confidence percentage, no inference about spending habits or discipline.

what_the_numbers_show: $1,800 is roughly 53% of one month's take-home pay.
No other figures were supplied, so nothing else can be calculated.
what_is_missing: Monthly fixed expenses (rent, utilities, loan payments) — without these, disposable income is unknown.
Whether $1,800 is a lump sum due now or spread across time.
Current savings and whether an emergency fund is already in place.
Any other upcoming costs that compete with this expense.
questions_to_check: After your fixed monthly expenses, how much is left over each month?
Do you have savings you could use without depleting your emergency buffer?
Is the $1,800 all due at once, or can it be paid in stages over coming months?
Would paying for this require taking on debt or skipping another planned expense?
output.low_regret_next_step: Write down your fixed monthly expenses and subtract them from $3,400 — that leftover number is what actually tells you whether $1,800 is comfortable, tight, or out of reach right now.

cases.name: tip-unverified-norm
cases.guards: Arithmetic from the supplied bill only. The local norm is NOT verified, so it belongs in check_first, not asserted in practical_answer. No invented service charge, auto-gratuity or party-size rule.

input.situation: Dinner out, service was slow but friendly

output.practical_answer: Tipping norms in Portugal are not standardized and vary by establishment and traveler background — check locally before deciding on a percentage. If you want to leave something, rounding up the bill or leaving a small amount is one common approach, but no specific figure can be stated as the expected norm here.
why: Service was slow, which may factor into how much, if anything, you leave.
Service was friendly, which some people weigh in the other direction.
Party of 4 — worth checking whether a service charge was already included on the bill.
check_first: Local tipping expectations vary; check the current norm for restaurant tipping in Portugal.
Verify whether a service charge or cover charge ('couvert') was already added to your €68 bill — this is common in Portuguese restaurants.
If a service charge is already included, an additional tip may not be expected at all.

cases.name: gift-budget-supplied
cases.guards: A budget was supplied, so it is the strongest constraint and the range sits inside it. No single correct amount, and no claim about what the recipient expects or will spend.

why_this_range: Your stated budget is $150, so the range sits at or below that ceiling.
A cousin is a close family relationship, which often calls for a more substantial gift than a coworker or acquaintance — though how close you actually are matters more than the label.
Wedding gifts typically cover more than a casual occasion, which pushes toward the upper portion of your available budget.
output.budget_check: The range lands entirely within your $150 budget. Spending at the top of the range ($150) is fully within what you said you can do, and $100 gives you a comfortable lower floor if you want breathing room.
output.social_context: What counts as an appropriate wedding gift for a cousin varies widely by region, family culture, and your personal closeness — there is no single standard. Some families give primarily cash or registry items; others prioritize sentimental or experience-based gifts. If your family has a pattern, that is worth more than any general norm.
output.if_you_want_to_spend_less: A thoughtful registry item in the $75–$100 range, especially something the couple specifically listed, reads as intentional rather than minimal — the registry choice itself signals that you paid attention.
output.if_you_want_to_spend_more: Going above $150 would let you cover a larger registry item, contribute meaningfully to a group gift, or give cash that edges closer to covering a tangible wedding expense — the difference is mostly scale, not kind.

cases.name: salary-no-target-supplied
cases.guards: The recruiting case, and the twelve leaps the 2026-09-04 pass removed. No target figure was supplied, so ask.amount MUST be empty. Being recruited is CONTEXT, not leverage — 'the company initiated the recruiting conversation', never 'recruited, not applying, which shifts the starting posture'. Remote is not a financial benefit unless the visitor made that comparison. Tenure is not institutional knowledge or reduced ramp time at a different company. A belief that pay is below market does not make current salary a floor. No invented headcount or revenue milestone as promotion criteria. Unquantified equity is 'difficult to evaluate', never 'means nothing'. No equity upside asserted. Market data is evidence, never the correct salary. Every if_they_push_back entry is labelled as a possibility, never as what this employer will do. A script may not claim research the visitor never said they did — it must be conditional on verifying a figure first. And no named compensation-data provider, because their current relevance is unverified.

input.situation: A startup recruiter reached out about a Senior Marketing Manager role, fully remote, with a director track mentioned and broader ownership. My current role is hybrid three days a week. I think I am underpaid for my market.
input.experience: 6 years B2B SaaS marketing, 4 at current company

what_you_have_to_work_with: The company initiated the recruiting conversation — you did not apply
Your current base is $115,000 with a hybrid three-days-a-week arrangement
Six years of B2B SaaS marketing experience, including four at your current company
The new role is fully remote and described as having broader ownership than your current position
A director track was mentioned in the recruiting conversation
what_you_still_need_to_know: Your target number — check current compensation data for comparable Senior Marketing Manager roles, remote, B2B SaaS, using more than one credible source before the conversation
What the director track actually means at this company — what would need to happen, who decides, and whether any timeline or review point is defined
The full compensation structure — base, bonus target and structure, equity terms and stage
Equity specifics — type, strike price, vesting schedule, cliff, and what the current cap table looks like — without these the equity component is difficult to evaluate

ask.basis: You have not yet supplied a target figure. Your basis for an ask would rest on your six years of B2B SaaS experience, the scope and ownership described for this role, and compensation data you verify before the conversation. Your current $115,000 base is a data point, not a floor — particularly if you believe it is already below market.
ask.script: Once you have verified a defensible figure from current compensation data for this level, scope, and remote status, you could say: 'Based on the scope of this role and the data I have looked at for comparable positions, I am targeting a base in the range of [your verified figure]. I want to make sure we are in the same conversation before we go further — does that work for you?'

if_they_push_back.situation: If they ask for your number first, before you are ready to give one
if_they_push_back.response: 'I want to make sure I understand the full scope and comp structure before I name a number — can you share the range you are working with for this role?'

if_they_push_back.situation: If the base they offer is lower than your target
if_they_push_back.response: 'I appreciate the offer. The base is a bit below where I need to be given the scope and what I have seen for comparable roles. Is there flexibility there, or room to discuss how the bonus or equity might bridge the gap?'

if_they_push_back.situation: If they lean on startup size or early-stage risk as a reason for a lower base
if_they_push_back.response: 'I understand the stage, and I want to evaluate the equity seriously once I have the full terms. For the base, I need it to be a number I can commit to regardless of how the equity plays out.'

if_they_push_back.situation: If they ask what would close the deal
if_they_push_back.response: 'A base of [your verified figure], a clear picture of the bonus structure, and enough detail on the equity to evaluate it alongside the cash comp — those three things together would let me make a confident decision.'

other_terms_you_may_want_to_raise: The director track — what it requires, who decides, and whether any review point is defined (you raised this)
Bonus structure — target percentage, what it is tied to, and how it has paid out historically
Equity terms — type, vesting, cliff, strike price, and current stage (you raised this)
Remote work setup — whether there is a home-office stipend or equipment provision, if that matters to you
Start date and any flexibility around it, if you have constraints

cases.name: family-no-dynamic-supplied
cases.guards: No family dynamic and no cultural context supplied. Nothing may infer guilt, obligation, favouritism, control or a 'real issue underneath the money' — the retired fields the_real_issue, emotional_stakes and if_guilt_trip must not reappear under any name.

input.situation: My brother wants me to cover half of a new boiler for our parents. I can manage about a third.

output.practical_issue: Your brother has asked you to pay half the cost of a new boiler for your parents, but you can only contribute a third. The gap between what he is asking and what you can offer needs to be bridged somehow.
what_is_known: Your brother wants you to cover half the boiler cost
You can manage roughly a third of the cost
The total cost of the boiler has not been supplied
what_needs_clarifying: What is the total cost, and what does each share actually come to in money?
Who covers the remaining portion if you contribute a third — your brother, your parents, or someone else?
Is there a deadline for when the money is needed?
Are other siblings or family members involved or expected to contribute?

conversation.opener: I want to help with the boiler. I have worked out what I can put in, and it comes to about a third of the cost rather than half.
key_points: Name your actual contribution amount once you know the total
Make clear this is what you can commit to, not a negotiating position
Ask directly how he sees the remaining share being covered
conversation.boundary_if_needed: I can put in a third and I want that to be my agreed share. I am not in a position to commit to half.
conversation.if_they_disagree: I understand that leaves a gap, and I am sorry I cannot do more right now. A third is genuinely what I can manage — can we work out together how to cover the rest?

cases.name: date-second-date
cases.guards: what_splitting_signals is gone. Nothing may say what any option signals about interest, independence, generosity, commitment or gender expectations — how_each_option_may_feel_or_function is conditional and about the evening, not the people. No confidence percentage.

input.situation: Second date, they suggested the restaurant

options.how_it_works: When the check arrives, one of you picks it up and says you have got it. The other person may accept or offer to cover next time.
options.how_each_option_may_feel_or_function: This may simplify the moment and avoid any arithmetic at the table. It may also leave the question of who pays next time open, which could come up before the date ends.

options.how_it_works: You each pay half, either by asking for two checks or by one person paying and the other transferring their share afterward.
options.how_each_option_may_feel_or_function: This closes the bill cleanly with no lingering imbalance. If the two orders were very different in price, one person may end up slightly over or underpaying, which may or may not matter to either of you.
options.script: Want to just split it down the middle?

options.how_it_works: One person covers this bill; it is understood the other covers a future one. This requires at least a loose verbal agreement so both people are operating on the same assumption.
options.how_each_option_may_feel_or_function: It keeps individual checks off the table tonight while spreading cost across time. It only works smoothly if both people are clear on the arrangement — a brief explicit mention avoids ambiguity later.
options.script: I will grab this one — you can get the next one.

options.how_it_works: Before you order, you briefly agree on how you will handle the bill, so neither of you is navigating it cold when it arrives.
options.how_each_option_may_feel_or_function: This removes the guesswork at the end of the meal. Raising it early may feel more natural for some people and slightly formal for others — there is no way to predict how your specific companion will experience it.
options.script: Just so we are not figuring it out later — want to split, or do you have a preference?

what_you_told_me: The other person suggested the restaurant.
what_is_not_established: What the other person expects around payment on a date.
Whether the other person has any assumption based on who suggested the venue.
Either person's preference, comfort level, or financial situation.
output.if_it_comes_up_awkwardly: If the check lands and nobody moves, a simple 'How do you want to handle this?' names the moment without pressure and lets the other person respond however they prefer.

cases.name: cultural-two-backgrounds
cases.guards: The hardest case. Neither background establishes an expectation. Nothing may describe Korea, the US, or any culture as having one money rule, say what an action 'actually means in their culture', or output a culture-clash score. Only expectations the visitor actually described may appear in what_you_have_described.

input.situation: His parents are visiting and want to take us out to dinner. I usually offer to split.

what_you_have_described: You typically offer to split the bill when dining out
His parents have invited you both to dinner
output.possible_mismatch: You have described your own default habit but not your partner's expectation or his parents' expectation — so it is not yet clear whether anyone's expectations actually differ. The mismatch may exist, or everyone may be on the same page.
what_not_to_assume: Growing up in Seoul does not establish what his parents expect around who pays
Issuing the invitation does not necessarily mean his parents expect to pay the full bill
Your partner's background does not tell you what norm he personally holds now
Your usual habit of splitting does not mean it is expected or preferred in this situation
questions_to_make_explicit: Ask your partner: 'When your parents invite us out, do they usually expect to cover the bill, or does splitting feel normal to them?'
Ask your partner: 'Would it feel awkward to them if I offered to split tonight?'
Ask yourself: 'Am I offering to split because I genuinely want to, or because I feel obligated to?'
output.bridge: Ask your partner before the dinner, not at the table — he is your best source of what his parents actually expect. Whatever he tells you, you can follow his lead in the moment without anyone having to guess.
output.script: Before we go tonight, I want to make sure I handle the bill in a way that feels right to your parents. When they invite us out, do they usually expect to pay, or is splitting welcome? I am happy either way — I just do not want to do something that feels off to them.

cases.name: charity-tax-question
cases.guards: tax_note must say only that treatment depends on jurisdiction and recipient status and should be verified. No deductibility claim of any kind.

input.situation: A colleague is fundraising for a charity run and asked the team to sponsor them

why: A colleague ask carries mild social weight but no real obligation; this is a voluntary contribution to their personal fundraising effort.
The cause and the amount are entirely your call — nothing about this situation requires a specific response.
Keeping it modest protects you if similar asks come from other colleagues in future.
output.amount_guidance: For a colleague relationship with no closer context, a token amount — whatever feels easy and forgettable in your budget — is typically the comfortable zone. If you have a number in mind, that instinct is usually the right guide. There is no correct figure here.
output.tax_note: Tax treatment depends on jurisdiction and the recipient's status; verify before relying on a deduction.
output.script: Hey, happy to support — I have just sponsored you. Good luck with the run! If you would prefer to decline: Thanks so much for sharing this — I am keeping a tight rein on extras at the moment, but I hope the run goes brilliantly.
output.if_they_push: I appreciate the cause, but I am not able to add anything right now — hope the team does well on the day.

cases.name: inheritance-split-question
cases.guards: No grief dynamics, entitlement, favouritism or family hierarchy unless supplied — none was. No jurisdiction-specific legal or tax conclusion: those belong in needs_professional_confirmation. It must not decide that equal or equitable is objectively correct.

input.situation: Three of us are dividing our mother house. One sibling lived there and cared for her for the last two years.

output.arrangement_considered: Three siblings are dividing their mother's house. One sibling lived there and provided care for the final two years, raising a question about whether that contribution should affect how the house is split.

principles_in_tension.pulls_toward: Each sibling receives one third of the estate regardless of circumstances
The caregiving sibling may have preserved the asset and delayed or avoided care facility costs, suggesting a larger share
Whatever the will says or whatever your mother expressed governs, overriding informal fairness arguments either way
The resident sibling absorbed real costs in time, income opportunity, and daily burden that the other two did not

facts_that_matter: What the will says, if one exists — it may already resolve the split or specify nothing about the house
Whether any informal agreement was made with your mother about compensation for the caregiving arrangement
Whether the caregiving sibling paid rent, contributed to mortgage or maintenance, or lived rent-free
Whether the caregiving sibling gave up employment or other income to provide care
Whether there are other assets in the estate that could offset an unequal split of the house
needs_professional_confirmation: Whether the will, if one exists, gives the executor discretion or already determines how the house is handled
Whether a caregiver's contribution can be formalised as a claim against the estate in your jurisdiction
Tax consequences of transferring, selling, or one sibling buying out the others
Whether any informal promise your mother made about the house has legal standing

conversation.opener: Before we talk numbers, I think we should each say what we think the caregiving arrangement means for how we divide the house — because I want us to be explicit about it rather than assume we all see it the same way.
what_to_clarify: Did Mum ever say anything to any of us about how she wanted the house handled, or what she felt was fair given the care arrangement?
Did the sibling who lived there have any understanding with Mum — spoken or otherwise — about what that would mean for their share?
Is any of us in a position where we need the house sold quickly, or does everyone have flexibility on timing?
Are we open to a split that is not equal thirds, and if so, how do we agree on what is fair?
